The invention relates to a method for producing composite webs or composite sheets, consisting of at least a first lower cover layer (1) of metal, a second upper cover layer (2) of metal, and a core layer (3) of plastic, which is arranged between the cover layers (1, 2) and is integrally bonded thereto, wherein a first metal strip (4) for the lower cover layer (1), a second metal strip (5) for the upper cover layer (2), and a plastic web (6) for the core layer (3) are brought together and are integrally bonded to each other by the application of pressure and/or heat. The method is characterized in that the first metal strip (4) and the second metal strip (5) are each continuously coated with an adhesion promoter in a pretreatment line (V) and then wound and that the first metal strip (4), the second metal strip (5), and the plastic web (6) are then brought together in a laminating line that is separate from the pretreatment line (L) and are continuously bonded to each other by the application of pressure and heat in order to form a composite web.

outputs.L3:
The invention relates to a method for producing composite webs or composite sheets comprising two metal cover layers and a plastic core layer. In the finished composite material, the plastic core layer is arranged between a lower metal cover layer and an upper metal cover layer and is integrally bonded to both metal cover layers. This results in a multilayer composite structure in which the metal layers provide strength, rigidity, and surface properties, while the plastic core layer contributes, for example, to weight reduction and specific functional characteristics.

In the method, a first metal strip, a second metal strip, and a plastic web are brought together in such a way that the plastic web is positioned between the two metal strips. The layers are then bonded to one another by applying pressure and/or heat. Through this bonding step, the plastic core layer adheres to the opposing inner surfaces of the two metal cover layers, thereby forming a continuous composite web. The composite web may subsequently be processed further, for example by cooling, trimming, winding, or cutting into sheets.

Before the laminating step, each of the metal strips is continuously coated with an adhesion promoter in a separate pretreatment line. The adhesion promoter is applied to the surface of the respective metal strip that will later face the plastic core layer. After coating, the treated metal strips are wound into coils. This pretreatment makes it possible to prepare the metal strips in advance and to store or transport them before they are used in the subsequent laminating process.

In a later process step, the coated first and second metal strips are unwound together with the plastic web in a separate laminating line. The three layers are continuously brought together, with the plastic web arranged between the coated sides of the metal strips. By the application of pressure and/or heat, the adhesion promoter promotes a durable integral bond between the metal cover layers and the plastic core layer. In this way, a continuous composite web is produced efficiently and reliably, with the pretreatment of the metal strips being separated from the final laminating operation.
outputs.L4:
A method is provided for producing metal-plastic composite webs or sheets in which two metal cover layers are permanently bonded to a plastic core layer by the combined action of pressure and heat. In this process, a first metal strip and a second metal strip are used as outer cover layers, while a plastic web, film, or sheet is introduced between them as the core material. The three layers are brought together in a laminating device and are joined to form a multilayer composite material.

A central feature of the method is that the two metal strips are not coated with adhesion promoter directly in the laminating line. Instead, each metal strip is first treated in a separate, continuous pretreatment line. In this pretreatment operation, an adhesion-promoting layer is applied to the surface of the metal strip that will later face the plastic core. After application of the adhesion promoter, the coated metal strip may be dried, cured, or otherwise conditioned as required. The pretreated metal strips are then wound into coils and stored or transported for later use.

During subsequent production of the composite web or sheet, the two pretreated metal coils are unwound and fed continuously toward the laminating station. At the same time, the plastic core web is supplied between the two metal strips. The adhesion-promoter-coated sides of the metal strips are oriented toward the plastic core. The layer arrangement is then passed through heated pressure rolls, a press, or another suitable laminating device. Under the influence of heat and pressure, the plastic core bonds firmly to the adhesion-promoting layers on the metal cover sheets, producing a stable metal-plastic-metal composite.

Because the adhesion promoter is applied in advance in a separate continuous pretreatment line, the laminating process itself can be carried out more efficiently. The metal strips can be coated under optimized conditions independently of the lamination speed and the plastic-core processing requirements. This improves process reliability, ensures uniform application of the adhesion promoter, and allows the laminating line to operate continuously without interruption for coating, drying, or curing steps.

The method is particularly advantageous for industrial-scale production of composite sheets or webs, since pretreated metal coils can be prepared in advance and then used as needed. This enables high production speeds, consistent bonding quality, and improved adhesion between the metal cover layers and the plastic core. The resulting composite material combines the mechanical strength, surface properties, and barrier characteristics of metal with the low weight and functional properties of the plastic core.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest and most common words in the English language, yet it plays an important role in communication. As a definite article, “the” points to something specific. When we say “a book,” we may mean any book, but when we say “the book,” we mean a particular one that the listener or reader can identify.

This simple word helps create clarity. It connects ideas, identifies objects, and gives sentences direction. For example, “the sun,” “the world,” and “the truth” all suggest something known or unique. Without “the,” English would feel less precise and less natural.

Although it is often overlooked, “the” is essential in everyday speech and writing. It proves that even the smallest words can carry great meaning.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for an invention about manufacturing metal-plastic-metal composite sheets where both metal strips are coated with adhesion promoter in a separate pretreatment line before lamination.
counterfactuals.output: A method for manufacturing a metal-plastic-metal composite sheet is disclosed. A first metal strip and a second metal strip are each supplied to a pretreatment line separate from a lamination line, where at least one surface of each strip is cleaned and coated with an adhesion promoter. The coated strips are optionally dried, cured, and/or wound into coils for intermediate storage or transport. In the lamination line, the pretreated metal strips are unwound and guided on opposite sides of a thermoplastic core layer, and the assembly is heated and pressed to bond the metal strips to the core layer, thereby forming a composite sheet. Pretreating both metal strips outside the lamination line permits independent control of coating conditions, reduces complexity and contamination in the lamination line, and improves reproducibility of adhesion between the metal skins and the plastic core.

counterfactuals.prompt: Create a technical patent description paragraph for a method of making aluminum composite material with lower and upper metal cover layers and a plastic core, emphasizing separate pretreatment and laminating lines.
counterfactuals.output: A method for producing an aluminum composite material comprising a plastic core layer arranged between a lower metal cover layer and an upper metal cover layer, wherein the lower and upper metal cover layers are supplied as separate aluminum strip materials to at least one pretreatment line that is operated independently of a laminating line. In the pretreatment line, each aluminum strip is unwound, cleaned, chemically and/or electrolytically pretreated, optionally provided with a conversion coating, primer, adhesion-promoting layer, or protective coating, and subsequently dried and rewound or transferred to an intermediate storage region. The pretreated lower and upper metal cover layers are thereafter supplied to a laminating line that is physically and functionally separate from the pretreatment line, the laminating line feeding the plastic core layer between the pretreated metal cover layers and bonding the layers together under heat and/or pressure to form a continuous aluminum composite strip or panel. By separating pretreatment from lamination, the surface preparation parameters of the metal cover layers can be adjusted independently of the laminating conditions, thereby improving adhesion, corrosion resistance, process flexibility, and throughput while permitting different pretreatments or coatings to be applied to the lower and upper cover layers before they are combined with the plastic core.
